about: Where this SDK's normalizer, replaying a shared recording from rius-semconv, produces something other than the recording's stored expected result. Each entry is reviewed and says why it is allowed. tests/test_conformance.py fails on any difference not listed here and on a listed one that no longer occurs, so fixing a difference means deleting its entry in the same change. `key` is an attribute key, or one of `events`, `status`, `name`, `kind`, or `scenario` for a recorded scenario with no expected result; `"*"` covers every difference in the family.

differences.reason: The TypeScript SDK is the reference here: it starts @ai-sdk/otel's spans through its aggregatingTracer and moves a run's total usage off the invoke_agent span to rius.aggregated_usage.*. The Python SDK has no @ai-sdk/otel producer (the AI SDK is JavaScript-only) and cannot tell an aggregate from the span alone, so it keeps the usage.

The TypeScript SDK is the reference here: @ai-sdk/otel writes the reasoning split only under the AI SDK's spelling, and the TypeScript SDK maps it (a model call's to gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens, a step's and a run's to rius.aggregated_usage.*). The Python SDK has no ai.* mapping (the AI SDK is JavaScript-only, so it never sees these spans live), so the key passes through.
As ai.usage.outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens, and on a step's or a run's span also as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens.

The TypeScript SDK is the reference here: its normalizer maps the AI SDK's ai.* dialect onto the conventions. The Python SDK has no ai.* mapping (the AI SDK is JavaScript-only, so it never sees these spans live), so the raw spans pass through.
